original_question: Describe all finite two-dimensional sails, and thereby all corresponding continued fractions, in the geometric multidimensional-continued-fraction setting.
target_in_paper: §3.3, Problem 7: "Describe all finite two-dimensional sails (and the corresponding continued fractions)."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly points to the classification of entire finite two-dimensional sails, together with the associated continued fractions, in geometric multidimensional continued-fraction theory. It also avoids drifting to neighboring but different questions such as which polygons occur as faces or which periodic torus decompositions occur.
missing_details: The paper places this problem in the rational-cone case [R], not in the algebraic/periodic case [A] or the nonperiodic cases [D] and [G].
In §3.1, a rational cone is defined as a cone whose every 1-edge contains an integer point; the paper states that sails of such cones have finitely many faces of all dimensions.
The ambient setting is real space with the integer lattice Z^n, and the natural equivalence notion throughout the paper is integer congruence under affine lattice-preserving transformations.
The problem is stated as open for Klein sails, Minkowski-Voronoi polyhedra, and most other continued-fraction constructions in the rational-cone setting; the draft does not mention this scope.
To be stand-alone, the question should say what a sail is in this paper: the boundary object attached to a cone of a hyperplane arrangement in the geometric multidimensional-continued-fraction sense.

The phrase "two-dimensional sail" should be understood as the sail itself being a two-dimensional polyhedral object/surface; otherwise it can be confused with the classical ordinary-continued-fraction picture discussed earlier in the paper.
The local context in §3.3 is the search for a complete and precise combinatorial description/invariant of sails; the draft does not make that intended classification strength explicit.

The paper does not give a separate proved equivalent reformulation beyond the parenthetical phrase "and the corresponding continued fractions," so a refined version should not introduce a new equivalence claim.
refined_question: Within the rational-cone case of geometric multidimensional continued fractions in real space with lattice Z^n, describe, up to affine integer-lattice congruence, all finite two-dimensional sails—that is, all two-dimensional sails arising from cones whose every 1-edge contains an integer point, so that the sail has finitely many faces—for the standard constructions considered in the paper, in particular Klein sails and Minkowski-Voronoi polyhedra, and determine the corresponding continued fractions.
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft: §3.3, Problem 7 states almost verbatim the same question. I made explicit only the hidden assumptions supplied by the nearby context: §3.3 says the problem is open for Klein sails, Minkowski-Voronoi polyhedra, and most other continued fractions in case [R]; §3.1 defines [R] as rational cones, for which sails are finite; §2 defines the sail framework and names the Klein and Minkowski-Voronoi models; and §1.1 supplies integer congruence as the paper's ambient equivalence notion. I did not broaden the question to face-classification (§3.2, Problem 5) or to periodic/algebraic torus decompositions (§3.3, Problem 11), because those are distinct neighboring problems.
